How to make a QR code for a Google Form

It takes two minutes, and most of the time goes into checking the form settings.

  1. Open your form in Google Forms and click Send.
  2. Choose the link option and copy the link. You can shorten it with the option shown in the same window.
  3. Paste the link into the field above and choose your colors.
  4. Download the PNG or SVG.
  5. Open the form with your QR code on a phone that is signed out to confirm anyone can respond.

Check these form settings first

Most failed form QR codes come from settings, not from the code.

  • Who can respond. If the form is limited to people in your organization, outsiders will be asked to sign in and may be blocked.
  • Sign-in requirements. Options that require a Google account or restrict to one response per person make the form harder for casual visitors.
  • Accepting responses. Make sure the form is not closed, or the code will lead to a closed message.
  • Form length. Phone users abandon long forms. Keep it short and use multiple choice where you can.
  • Test on mobile. Every question should be easy to answer with one hand.
Where to Use It

What people use Google Form QR codes for

Customer feedback

Put a code on receipts and tables for a quick survey.

Event RSVPs & sign-ins

Replace paper sign-up sheets at the door.

Classroom quizzes

Share a quiz or exit ticket with a projected code.

Registration forms

Collect entries for classes, clubs and sports.

Volunteer & job applications

Post a code on a notice board or flyer.

Order & booking forms

Let customers place a request from a poster.

Privacy and data

When people fill in your form, you become responsible for how you handle their answers. Only ask for what you need, say what you will use it for, and follow the privacy rules that apply where you operate.

This tool only creates the QR code. It does not see your form or the responses.
